rows.claim: The at lift code block: at(prefix::String, p::TrimProblem) with reads = at(prefix, p.reads)
rows.evidence: src/trim.jl:122-127 takes AbstractString and lifts reads only when problem.reads isa Reads, otherwise passes it through; probe:71 prints NamedTuple() for a problem whose reads is (;); test/test_trim.jl:978-986
rows.fix: In the block, write `at(prefix::AbstractString, p::TrimProblem)` and `reads = p.reads isa Reads ? at(prefix, p.reads) : p.reads,  #inert selector data: the prefix is prepended to the read set's mount chain; a malformed reads passes through so trim!'s setup names it as TrimProblemInvalid :not_a_read_set`. Nothing in the log records the pass-through (D-278 covers only the empty prefix); code_map.md:1478 alone does.
rows.note: The prose at 14153-14156 says the lift prepends to a read set, which stays true.

rows.evidence: src/conditions.jl:705 throws DiagnosticError(UninitializedInputs(...)), one diagnostic in a fail-fast carrier; probe:17 prints DiagnosticError{UninitializedInputs} and the descriptor body reports policy fail-fast; probe:21 and probe:23 show the same carrier for linearize about and trim!; src/descriptor.jl:98 reads policy off the carrier type; test/test_assembly.jl:103 and test/test_trim.jl:631 expect DiagnosticError{UninitializedInputs}
rows.fix: Appendix C entry: `Error · service, pre-write · fail-fast.` and say the one diagnostic names every uncovered root face in declaration order. §14.6 (spec.md:13503) says `one collected, declaration-ordered diagnostic` and wants the same rewording, for example `one declaration-ordered diagnostic naming every uncovered face`. The alternative is a defect fix, wrapping the diagnostic in a Vector{Diagnostic} carrier in assert_total, which changes the carrier type the tests match on.
rows.note: Appendix C defines collected as thrown as one carrier with its siblings. The code gathers the faces into one value, not into a collection.
